headline: A London Assembly committee has told Transport for London not to approve a full launch of driverless taxis until safety is tightened, saying the city is not ready.
score_reason: Pool 6 kept: the report was covered on 11-12 Oct 2026, inside the window, and the article's facts match the headline; it is a recommendation, not a decision.
importance_line: It adds official doubt to plans to launch driverless taxis from operators including Waymo, Wayve and Baidu in London, which matters to Londoners who ride, drive or cross the streets they would use and to private hire drivers worried about their jobs, but the committee has only urged a delay and no operator has yet passed the national safety approval that comes first.
summary: The London Evening Standard reports that the London Assembly's transport committee, a panel of the elected Assembly that scrutinizes the city's transport policy, said it had not heard enough evidence to welcome driverless passenger services, citing doubts about help for passengers in emergencies, extra congestion and pollution, and the limited power of Transport for London (TfL) to cap vehicle numbers or revoke an operator's license. It made 13 recommendations, and a YouGov poll cited in its report found 29 percent of Londoners in favor and 42 percent opposed, while TfL officials say they are "not in a rush" to approve the technology and, according to the Standard, no operator has yet completed the national safety approval process.
notes: Read in full via the Standard (fulltext). The Times also covered the report on 11 Oct 2026 (headline seen in Google News only).
